tables.title: Debug port registers
tables.text_helper: Table 579, "Debug port registers", in section 49.3.3 (Debug port registers) on page 2424. Columns: Address, A(3:2) value, R/W, Description. 9 data row(s). Notes: 1. Access to the AP ABORT register from the JTAG-DP is done using the ABORT instruction.; 2. Only accessible via SW-DP. Register is “reserved” via JTAG-DP.

rows: DP_DPIDR contains the IDCODE for the debug port.

DP_ABORTR(1) aborts the current AP transaction. This register is also used to clear 
the error flags in the DP_CTRLSTATR register.

If DP_SELECTR.DPBANKSEL[3:0] = 0x0, DP_CTRLSTATR controls the DP and 
provides status information.

If DP_SELECTR.DPBANKSEL[3:0] = 0x1, DP_DLCR(2) controls the operating mode 
of the SWD data link.

If DP_SELECTR.DPBANKSEL[3:0] = 0x2, DP_TARGETIDR provides target 
identification information.

If DP_SELECTR.DPBANKSEL[3:0] = 0x3, DP_DLPIDR(2) provides the SWD protocol 
version.

DP_RESENDR(2) returns the value that was returned by the last AP read or 
DP_RDBUFF read. Used in the event of a corrupted read transfer.

DP_SELECTR selects the access port, access port register bank, and DP register at 
address 0x4.

DP read buffer register (DP_RDBUFFR): 
– Via JTAG-DP, this register allows the debugger to get the final result after a 
sequence of operations (without requesting new JTAG-DP operation)
– Via SW-DP, this register contains the result of the preceding AP read access, 
allowing a new AP access to be avoided.
notes: 1. Access to the AP ABORT register from the JTAG-DP is done using the ABORT instruction.
2. Only accessible via SW-DP. Register is “reserved” via JTAG-DP.
